page: Amazon Web Services m7i.16xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at a base clock frequency of 3.2 GHz, delivering 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The processor includes 105 MB of L3 cache alongside hardware support for advanced vector and matrix acceleration instructions, including AVX-512, AMX-TILE, and AMX-INT8, alongside cryptographic extensions such as VAES and SHA-NI. System memory totals 256 GB of DDR5 operating at 6000 MHz, providing a standard 1:4 ratio of 4 GB of memory per core.

Hardware benchmark results reflect strong compute density and memory subsystem efficiency. In compute workloads, the instance achieves top-quartile performance across Geekbench multi-core processing, code compilation via Clang, and PassMark extended instruction evaluations. The DDR5 memory configuration delivers up to 224.98 GB/s in large-block uncached read throughput and 94.16 GB/s in write bandwidth. Supported by AMX and AVX-512 extensions, CPU-based machine learning inference achieves strong throughput for medium-scale 7B language models, processing 251.73 prompt tokens per second and generating 35.74 tokens per second.

In operational profiles, the instance demonstrates high data handling rates, yielding 75.63 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations and over 76 GB/s in static web serving throughput. A primary architectural tradeoff is the absence of bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes across its 25 Gbps baseline network interface. Lacking discrete GPUs, heavy deep learning tasks remain constrained to smaller models. Overall, the resource ratio provides cost-efficient scaling for large in-memory databases, dense CI/CD build farms, enterprise backend applications, and CPU-driven inference pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services m7i.16xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and a 3.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8488C processor. Configured with 64 vCPUs (32 physical cores) and 256 GB of DDR5 memory running at 6000 MHz, the system maintains a balanced 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio. It features hardware acceleration for vector and matrix mathematics via AVX-512 and Intel AMX, while omitting dedicated GPUs and local storage in favor of a 25 Gbps baseline network link for storage attachment. Benchmark testing shows top-quartile results in multi-core compiling, encryption, database operations, and Redis throughput exceeding 75 million operations per second. Memory throughput reaches 224.98 GB/s in uncached read operations. The instance is suited for enterprise application backends, extensive CI/CD build environments, Redis caching nodes, and CPU-based language model inference.
